mainTopic: Giving up rights given by the חכמים, and whether a wife can claim she sold or gave a field only to please her husband
overview: This amud first explains that a person can give up an inheritance he has not received yet. It ties this to the rule of רבא: anyone who turns down a תקנת חכמים made for his benefit is listened to. The גמרא asks which kind of תקנה רבא meant. It answers with the ruling of רב הונא in the name of רב: a wife may tell her husband, 'Don't support me, and my earnings stay with me.' Then the גמרא returns to the משנה's rule that a husband gains no חזקה in his wife's field, which implies that proof of a sale or gift would help him. It challenges this: why can't the wife say she only signed to please her husband? It supports the challenge with a משנה in גיטין, where a wife's sale is canceled for exactly that reason. The גמרא answers with רבה בר רב הונא, who limits that claim to three special fields. The first is a field the husband wrote into her כתובה, and the rest of the list continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A person can give up a future inheritance, following רבא
steps.stepSummary: A person may set a condition that he will not inherit property he has not yet received. This follows רבא, who says anyone who turns down a תקנת חכמים made for his benefit is listened to.
steps.simpleTranslation: An inheritance that will come to a person from somewhere else: a person can set a condition that he will not inherit it. This follows רבא, who said: anyone who says 'I don't want a תקנת חכמים like this one' is listened to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why a person is allowed to give up a right he has not received yet, and it backs this up with a rule from רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Property that is not yours yet is easier to waive than property you already own, so you can say ahead of time that you won't take it. רבא adds a wider rule: a benefit the חכמים set up for you can be turned down. The words 'like this one' are left unclear, and the next step asks what they mean.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person may give up a future inheritance, and anyone may turn down a תקנת חכמים made for his benefit.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up the general idea that benefits the חכמים created for a person can be waived by that person.

steps.title: What does 'such as this' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which case רבא meant when he said 'such as this.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what example רבא had in mind. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא did not say his rule covers every תקנה. 'Such as this' points to one specific kind of case, and the גמרא wants to identify it.

keyTerms.meaning: What?
Such as this; like this case

phrases.english: What is meant by 'such as this'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what one phrase in רבא's statement means
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which example of a waivable תקנה רבא was pointing to

steps.title: A wife may refuse support and keep her earnings
steps.stepSummary: רבא meant the ruling of רב הונא in the name of רב: a wife may tell her husband she will not take his support and will not give him her earnings.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like what רב הונא said in the name of רב: a woman can tell her husband, 'I will not be supported by you, and I will not work for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'such as this' refers to the case of a wife who turns down her husband's support so that she can keep her own earnings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים set up an exchange: the husband supports his wife, and in return her earnings go to him. Since this was made mainly for her benefit, she may step out of it. That is the kind of תקנה רבא was talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: Being supported, meaning receiving food and support from the husband
Working, meaning her earnings go to the husband
She is able; she is allowed

steps.whatToRemember: A benefit the חכמים set up for someone, like a wife's right to support, can be turned down by that person.
steps.confusionAlert: Only the wife can make this choice, because the support was made for her. The husband cannot force it on her by saying, 'Keep your earnings, and I won't support you.'

phrases.english: Like that ruling of Rav Huna in the name of Rav,
as Rav Huna said in the name of Rav:
A woman can say to her husband:
'I will not be supported, and I will not work.'
phrases.notes: She means: don't support me, and in exchange my earnings stay with me.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The example is a wife giving up support in exchange for keeping her earnings, as רב הונא taught in the name of רב.

steps.title: Why can't the wife say she only did it to please her husband?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה implies that a husband with proof can win the field. The גמרא challenges this: the wife could say she only sold or gave it to keep her husband happy.
steps.simpleTranslation: So proof does work? But let her say, 'I only did it to please my husband!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now goes back to the משנה, which says a husband gains no חזקה in his wife's field. It notes the משנה implies proof would help him, and then challenges that idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband shows a bill of sale or a gift document, the משנה seems to say he wins. The challenge is that the document may mean nothing: a wife might sign just to keep the peace at home. If so, even proof should not help him.

keyTerms.meaning: Proof, such as a document showing he bought the field or received it as a gift
Let her say; why can't she claim
Pleasing someone; keeping him happy

phrases.english: So he does have the option of proof?
Let her say: 'Just to please

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה and challenges what can be inferred from it
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference from the משנה that a husband with proof of sale or gift owns his wife's field
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A wife's signature may not be sincere, since she could claim she signed only to please her husband. So even proof should not help him.

steps.title: Proof from a sale that is canceled because the wife was pleasing her husband
steps.stepSummary: A משנה in גיטין says that if someone bought land from the husband and then bought the wife's rights in it, the sale is void, because she can say she only did it to please her husband. The same claim should work here.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't we learn in a משנה: if a person bought from the husband and then went back and bought from the wife, his purchase is void? This shows that she can say, 'I only did it to please my husband.' Here too, let her say, 'I only did it to please my husband!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its challenge with a משנה where a wife's sale is canceled because of the 'I was pleasing my husband' claim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the wife sells her rights in the land, the rights her כתובה gives her for later. That sale is canceled because she only went along to make her husband happy. If that claim works there, it should also work against the husband's own proof here, which makes the challenge stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: Didn't we learn in a משנה? This introduces a source
His purchase is void
This shows that
Here too

steps.whatToRemember: The 'I did it to please my husband' claim can cancel a wife's sale. That makes it hard to see how a husband's proof could help him with his wife's field.

steps.title: The wife's claim only works for three special fields
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה in גיטין was already limited by רבה בר רב הונא. The wife's claim 'I only did it to please my husband' applies only to three special fields. The first is a field the husband wrote into her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it already said about that משנה that רבה בר רב הונא taught: this rule is needed only for those three fields? One is a field that the husband wrote for her in her כתובה...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by quoting רבה בר רב הונא, who limits the wife's 'pleasing my husband' claim to three special fields. It names the first field here, and the list continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 used the משנה in גיטין to say a wife can always claim she sold only to please her husband. רבה בר רב הונא narrows that rule to three special kinds of fields, such as a field set aside in her כתובה. So in our משנה, where the field is not one of these special fields, her claim does not work, and the husband's proof that he bought it or got it as a gift stands.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it already said about it? This brings in a known teaching that answers the question.
It was only needed for... This limits a rule to a narrow case.
Fields
The marriage contract that guarantees the wife's payment

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבה בר רב הונא is disagreeing with the משנה in גיטין. He is explaining that the משנה was only talking about these three special fields all along.
steps.whyThisMatters: This limit lets both משניות stand. The wife's claim protects her only for special fields tied to her rights, not for all of her property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4 by limiting the proof brought in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the cited source to specific cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The wife can always claim she sold or gave up her rights only to please her husband, for any field.
steps.terutzMaskana: That claim works only for three special fields, such as a field written into her כתובה. So it does not weaken the משנה's ruling here.
